name: Smartcat
tagline: Manage translation jobs and approved machine translation without recreating its marketplace

pricing.notes: Pricing is usage or sales based; canonical monthly amount is null.

tiers.name: Forever Free
tiers.limits: Unlimited users, projects and languages; CAT editor, unlimited Translation Memory storage and glossaries; initial AI balance only
tiers.notes: Initial Smartword allocation is one-time and expires; core workspace remains free.

tiers.name: Adapt
tiers.limits: Unlimited users; Chief of Staff plus Content Translator and Content Writer AI Co-workers; annual Smartwords allowance varies by contract

tiers.name: Accelerate
tiers.limits: Unlimited users; adds Reviewer and Marketplace collaboration; annual Smartwords allowance varies by contract

tiers.name: Anticipate
tiers.limits: Unlimited users; adds Content Update and QA Co-workers, API, SSO/2FA and reporting

tiers.name: Autonomous
tiers.limits: Unlimited users; all Co-workers, parallel/branching workflows, 7 hierarchical workspaces and enterprise governance

pricing.freeTierCaps: Unlimited users, projects and languages; initial AI balance is 15,000 Smartwords for corporate-email trials (14 days) or 3,000 for non-corporate-email trials (7 days), then AI use needs a top-up or paid plan
pricing.billingTerms: paid plans are annual only at published starting prices; consumption is based on Smartwords, not seats
pricing.hiddenCosts: Smartwords expire at renewal and extra Smartwords are paid; Marketplace commission is 20% on Forever Free and lower on paid plans; AI dubbing consumes 10 Smartwords per word and OCR image translation costs 1,000 Smartwords per image.

verdictSummary: A consolation build is possible, but the paid product's decisive value sits outside a solo rebuild. For Smartcat, manage translation jobs and approved machine translation without recreating its marketplace. The hard boundary is translator marketplace, payments, vendor management, ai, and enterprise workflow, plus translation memory, collaboration, and deployment integrations.
coreLoopDIY: Manage translation jobs and review work with approved machine translation, preserve context, import and export standard files, and publish approved strings without recreating a marketplace.
requirements: optional DeepL or OpenAI API key
whatYouLose: translator marketplace, payments, vendor management, AI, and enterprise workflow
moatNotes: translation memory, collaboration, and deployment integrations
ongoingBurden: file formats, placeholders, plural rules, screenshots, context, permissions, review, glossary, machine translation, sync, and backups
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Smartcat because localization teams pay because language context, review discipline, translators, and release integrations are the hard parts. The recurring cost buys file formats, placeholders, plural rules, screenshots, context, permissions, review, glossary, machine translation, sync, and backups, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Tolgee
priorArt.desc: Active open-source localization platform with translation memory and in-context tooling.

alternatives.name: MateCat
alternatives.desc: Free hosted translation jobs with memory, machine translation, sharing and an optional professional marketplace.

facts.install: Use the free hosted service, or follow the manual Ubuntu server installation guide
facts.engines: The default hosted template uses the public MyMemory translation memory and ModernMT Lite; MateCat also supports project-specific translation memories and configurable MT engines.
facts.dataFormat: On the hosted service, source files, segments, translation memories, project state, and output files reside on MateCat's servers; self-hosted data resides in MySQL plus the server's storage and supporting services.
facts.gapVsPaid: MateCat covers CAT editing and machine translation, but its marketplace, vendor procurement, payments, team administration, document AI, and end-to-end job management are much thinner than Smartcat's.
facts.setupBlocker: None for the hosted service; self-hosting is a specialist stack involving Ubuntu, Apache, PHP, MySQL, Redis, ActiveMQ, Node, certificates, compiled assets, and long-running daemons.

alternatives.name: OmegaT
alternatives.desc: A dependable desktop CAT tool for jobs, memory, glossaries and approved machine translation; no freelancer bazaar included.

facts.install: Download the Windows/macOS/Linux desktop package; most bundles include the required Java runtime
facts.engines: Can query configured machine-translation services and plugins, including documented connectors for DeepL, LibreTranslate, Moses, NICT TexTra, and other provider integrations.
facts.dataFormat: Each translation job is an ordinary project folder containing source and target files, translation memories and glossaries; the live translation memory is project_save.tmx under the omegat folder and nothing is stored by OmegaT in a vendor cloud.
facts.gapVsPaid: OmegaT is a local translator's CAT tool with no shared cloud workspace, vendor marketplace, assignment workflow, procurement, payments, or live project management.

alternatives.name: Weblate
alternatives.desc: Handles collaborative software-translation jobs with memory and review, but wisely does not impersonate Smartcat's marketplace.

facts.install: Hosted Weblate signup or the official Docker Compose deployment
facts.engines: Machine translation can connect to OpenAI/Azure OpenAI, DeepL, Google Cloud, Amazon Translate, Microsoft Translator, LibreTranslate, Baidu, Yandex, and other documented services.
facts.dataFormat: Translations, users, review state, memory, glossaries, and settings live in PostgreSQL; cloned source repositories and uploaded files live in persistent server volumes, with Valkey/Redis used for queues and caches.
facts.gapVsPaid: Weblate is optimized for collaborative software localization and does not replace Smartcat's document-job intake, freelancer marketplace, vendor procurement, payments, and broader business translation workflow.
facts.setupBlocker: Cloud hosting is free only for qualifying libre projects; the general free route requires Docker, PostgreSQL, Valkey/Redis, domain/TLS, mail, repository credentials, backups, and upgrades.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Platform plan and a small-team string-management system DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a closest honest personal substitute for Smartcat in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, Drizzle ORM, and one optional machine-translation API; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: manage translation jobs and review work with approved machine translation, preserve context, import and export standard files, and publish approved strings without recreating a marketplace.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Implement projects, locales, keys, namespaces, descriptions, screenshots, translations, and review status.
Import and export JSON, YAML, PO, and XLIFF while preserving placeholders and plural forms.
Add glossary checks, missing-string filters, translation memory, comments, and reviewer assignment.
Use machine translation only on selected strings and show provider, cost, and source text before approval.
Provide token-authenticated pull and push endpoints for CI with an immutable change log.
Add backups, locale deletion safeguards, and a pseudo-localization preview.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Do not claim to reproduce proprietary data, network liquidity, regulated access, or frontier infrastructure.
Deliberately leave out a translator labor marketplace.
Deliberately leave out a global website translation proxy.
Deliberately leave out enterprise integrations, legal translation assurance, and round-the-clock support.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
